title: Miso Soup with Halloumi and Pak Choi
subtitle: A hearty miso broth with grilled halloumi and greens
excerpt: A warming miso broth built on chicken stock with pak choi and spring onion, finished with golden cubes of pan-fried halloumi. Simple enough for a weeknight and more substantial than a traditional dashi-based miso soup.
sourceNotes: Miso soup is a Japanese staple eaten at almost every meal. This version adapts the basic structure of a dashi-free miso broth, using chicken stock and halloumi in place of the traditional tofu and kombu, making it more accessible with standard supermarket ingredients.

content.text: Do not add the miso directly to boiling liquid. Take the pan off the heat, dissolve the miso in a ladle of broth, then stir it back in. This preserves the flavour.
Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat. Add the halloumi cubes. Cook for 2 minutes per side until golden. Set aside.
Bring the chicken stock to a gentle simmer in a large saucepan.
Add the pak choi. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat. Spoon the miso paste into a small ladle.
Add a ladleful of hot broth to the miso and whisk until dissolved.
Stir the dissolved miso back into the pot.
Ladle into bowls. Add the halloumi cubes and spring onion.
Finish with a small drizzle of sesame oil.

items.cause: The miso amount was too low or it was boiled away.
items.fix: Add another tablespoon of miso dissolved in a ladle of broth.

items.symptom: Halloumi is rubbery rather than golden.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough when the halloumi went in.
items.fix: Use a very hot dry pan and do not move the cubes for 2 full minutes.
